rationale: Stages of senile cataract maturation — distinguishing immature, mature, and hypermature by iris shadow test is a classic AK Khurana trap
Lens metabolism — the avascular lens relies entirely on aqueous humour; students confuse this with blood supply
A-scan biometry for IOL power calculation — Parsons' classic preoperative assessment question; students confuse keratometry and A-scan roles
Informed consent — students must understand that routine consent covers only the specific eye to be operated and PCO risk must be explicitly disclosed
Phacoemulsification vs ECCE indications — a high-yield NMC trap distinguishing the modern gold standard from indications for older techniques
Posterior capsule opacification → Nd:YAG capsulotomy: the most common late complication of ECCE/phaco; students must know mechanism and correct treatment
Optical correction of aphakia — classic Parsons' ranking: IOL > contact lens > aphakic spectacles; students must know WHY spectacles are least preferred
Paediatric aphakia — contact lens is first-line in infants; IOL in very young children is controversial due to refractive shift with eye growth
IMG pre-operative role — instilling mydriatics; students must know the correct drug, timing, and purpose for cataract surgery preparation
Post-operative endophthalmitis recognition — the most feared complication; IMGs must know the 48-hour rule
